comment: The assistant had a pretty good success rate of doing what I asked. But as someone who has worked with this software for 5+ years it is just easier and quicker for me to do it myself. It is probably more beneficial to someone with less experience who doesn't know where everything is. If I was a new user using this to help me learn the software, I would like for it to go more slowly and clearly highlight what it was changing to execute my requests. I also think the nested menus of a DAW make it harder to validate that the system worked as intended (for things like adding delay to vocals that are hidden on the main screen) when compared to assistants in text editors.

I was confused on how to add reverb via send/return. I couldnt find a way and the instructions directed me to insert them onto the tracks directly. This had me spend extra time doing this by hand, while the AI assistant seemed to be able to use the send/return just fine.

I like doing by hand for smaller, subtle tasks like panning, levels, effect parameters. I think the AI assistant was really helpful for tasks like create a track, name it, and presumably if I were running a complicated session with many inputs this would be invaluable to just explain these things by voice like I would to a studio assistant.

I had never tried mixing music before, and I found it fun. It was interesting to hear how the music sounded different after I made changes. The AI sometimes misheard my voice commands. I wasn’t sure how to pronounce some of the mixing terms, so making the changes by hand sometimes felt easier.
